name: Vermont
feeText: $295 before the entry of any divorce or annulment proceeding in the Superior Court; $90 if filed with a stipulation for a final order and one or both parties are residents ($180 if neither is a resident) (32 V.S.A. § 1431(b)(2)).

otherFees.what: Divorce complaint filed with a stipulation for a final order, at least one party resident (32 V.S.A. § 1431(b)(2))
Motion or petition to vacate or modify a child support order (32 V.S.A. § 1431(b)(5))

residency.text: A complaint may be brought if either party has resided in Vermont for six months or more, but no divorce may be decreed unless the plaintiff or defendant has resided in the State one year before the final hearing (15 V.S.A. § 592(a)).

waitingPeriod.text: A divorce decree is first a decree nisi and becomes absolute 90 days after entry, unless the court fixes an earlier date (15 V.S.A. § 554(a)).

separationText: No-fault ground: the spouses have lived apart for six consecutive months and resumption of marital relations is not reasonably probable (15 V.S.A. § 551(7)); fault grounds need no separation.

simplified.text: No separate summary procedure in statute; an uncontested complaint filed with a stipulation for a final order pays a reduced $90 fee (32 V.S.A. § 1431(b)(2)).
